tier_reason: README tables compare lz4_flex against lzzzz (C lz4 1.9.3) on 66KB JSON and 10MB dickens with rustc 1.69.0, AMD Ryzen 7 5900HX (boost off, 3 GHz) and the cargo bench invocation; Cargo.toml [profile.bench] sets opt-level 3, lto = true, codegen-units = 1, and benches/ (now benches/binggan_bench.rs, which still benchmarks lzzzz on compression_66k_JSON.txt and dickens.txt) holds the code.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.69.0 (84c898d65 2023-04-16); cargo bench --no-default-features (safe-encode/safe-decode off) and cargo bench (safe on); Cargo.toml [profile.bench]: opt-level = 3, lto = true, codegen-units = 1. C compiler used by lzzzz to build lz4 1.9.3 not stated.
corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 5900HX, Manjaro, CPU boost disabled, governor performance (README also says CPU 3GHZ)
corrections.claimed_speedup: 66KB JSON: lz4_flex unsafe 1615 MiB/s compress and 5512 MiB/s decompress vs lzzz (lz4 1.9.3) 1469 and 5313 MiB/s; 10MB dickens: 347 MiB/s compress and 2734 MiB/s decompress vs 324 and 2759 MiB/s. About 1.10x and 1.07x compression, 1.04x and 0.99x decompression (derived from page data); 'unchecked_decode' variant decompresses at 5973 and 3168 MiB/s (1.12x and 1.15x, derived from page data). Safe build is slower than C lz4 (1272/4540 and 259/2338 MiB/s).
corrections.caveats: Own benchmark on two inputs; README numbers date from v0.11.0 (2023-06-02) with rustc 1.69 and were produced by the old criterion bench, while HEAD now uses a binggan bench (benches/binggan_bench.rs). The win over C lz4 is small (about 4-10%) and needs the unsafe configuration; the default safe build is slower than C lz4, and the fastest decompress row disables checked-decode, which the crate says must only be used on trusted input. C compiler and flags for the lzzzz-built lz4 baseline are not stated. The same README also lists lz-fear and snap.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly. Metadata checked on github.com: MIT, 618 stars, 61 forks, not archived, not a fork; last commit 2026-08-11 (PR #234). Tier A kept on the strength of public bench code, rustc version, Cargo bench profile and CPU, but the margin over C lz4 is small.

tier_reason: First-party README tables against nim-lang/zip (a zlib wrapper) with CPU (Ryzen 5 5600X) and the nim command line, and public bench code (tests/bench.nim), but the Nim version, the backend C compiler and the zlib version/build of the baseline are all unstated, so it falls short of A.

corrections.baseline: zlib via the nim-lang/zip wrapper (zlib version and build unstated; tests/bench.nim comments say the zlib path 'Requires zlib1.dll' and the README command uses a Windows-style path, so the README's 'zlib found on a fresh Linux install' may not describe the run shown)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: nim c --gc:arc -d:release -r tests/benchmark.nim (README; the file is now tests/bench.nim). Nim version, backend C compiler and C flags not stated.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'around 1.5x - 2x faster than zlib found on a fresh Linux install'. Min-time rows, Zippy vs nim-lang/zip: uncompress alice29.txt.gz 0.233 vs 0.397 ms (1.70x), tor-list.gz 27.297 vs 36.613 ms (1.34x); compress best speed alice29.txt 0.643 vs 1.236 ms (1.92x), tor-list 26.106 vs 178.197 ms (6.8x); compress default alice29.txt 2.361 vs 5.726 ms (2.43x), urls.10K 13.364 vs 13.049 ms (0.98x), tor-list 409.542 vs 244.424 ms (0.60x, Zippy slower). Ratios derived from page data.
corrections.workload: Deflate/gzip decompression and raw-deflate compression (best speed and default levels) of small corpus files (alice29.txt, urls.10K, rfctest3, randtest3, paper-100k.pdf, geo.protodata, gzipfiletest.txt, tor-list) timed with the benchy timeIt macro in tests/bench.nim
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers. The comparison library is nim-lang/zip, a wrapper over a zlib whose version and build are unstated (bench comment says 'Requires zlib1.dll', suggesting a Windows run despite the README's Linux framing). Default-level compression is slower than zlib on the largest file (tor-list: 409.542 vs 244.424 ms) and about equal on urls.10K, so the '1.5-2x' summary holds for decompression, best-speed mode and small files, not for default-level compression of large inputs. Compression ratios are not reported. README links tests/benchmark.nim, which is now 404; the bench lives at tests/bench.nim. Nim version and C backend compiler missing.

notes: Numbers match the README. Downgraded A to C: compiler version, C backend and baseline zlib build are unstated. Metadata checked: MIT, 283 stars, not archived, not a fork; last commit 2026-09-30 (PR #111, a Huffman histogram overflow fix).

tier_reason: First-party README gives only 'up to 25%/50% faster than pako' percentages with no data, runtime, CPU or flags; npm test writes metrics to test/results but none are published.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table (pako = 1x): decompression 'Up to 25% faster', compression 'Up to 50% faster'; text says about 25% faster than UZIP.js. Sync ZIP compression 'compresses both more quickly and with a higher compression ratio than most compression software (even Info-ZIP, a C program)'; async mode 'over 3x the performance of virtually any other utility'. Against native zlib (Node bindings) the README itself says fflate is 'around 30% slower in decompression and 10% slower in compression'.
corrections.caveats: The win is against pako (a JS port of zlib), not native zlib: the README states fflate is about 30% slower than native zlib in decompression and 10% slower in compression, and that the native CompressionStream API ranges from 30% faster to 10% slower. Only 'up to' percentages, no data, Node version, CPU or flags; results of npm test (test/results) are not published. The 'beats Info-ZIP' and '3x' statements are unsupported by tables. Worth listing as the fast pure-JS option where native zlib is unavailable (browsers without a sync API).

notes: Kept as a JS-ecosystem entry: faster than pako, but by its own README slower than native zlib, which matters for a catalog benchmarked against zlib. Metadata checked: MIT (SheetJS-derived part 0BSD), about 3.0k stars, not archived, not a fork; last commit 2026-05-16 (v0.8.3).
